bio-research.SPLIT_VERDICT_2026-07-29: KEEP the plugin for its SERVERS; treat its SKILLS as DO-NOT-USE. SKILLS: 4 of 6 assume capability this business does not have — nextflow-development (nf-core rnaseq/sarek/atacseq on sequencing data), instrument-data-to-allotrope (lab instrument output), scvi-tools and single-cell-rna-qc (single-cell .h5ad/.h5). There is no wet lab, no instruments and no sequencing; following them produces work implying in-house capability that does not exist, which for a citation-traced biomedical business is the exact failure it sells against. Usable ONLY as reference over public data (GEO/SRA), never implying in-house sequencing or sample handling. scientific-problem-selection and start are generic/marginal. SERVERS: verified against connector-registry.json — pubmed, chembl, c-trials(->clinicaltrials-gov), ot(->open-targets-graphql) and owkin all DUPLICATE existing subprocess-mcp engine adapters; biorxiv(->biorxiv-medrxiv) and consensus are registered claude-host-mcp; and wiley, synapse, biorender, benchling are NOT REGISTERED AT ALL. Uninstalling would forfeit the only path to Wiley (paywalled full text) and BioRender (figures for $9,950+ reports) — that is the sole reason the plugin stays. The five duplicates must stay OUT of config/tool-prefetch-map.json; the engine has its own adapters and double-registering dilutes the Phase-30 grounded-citation ratio.
bio-research.FOUNDER_LANE_BRIDGE_2026-07-29: The Founder Lane (01-brand-system/founder-lane-2026-07-29.md) makes a second buyer real: medical-startup founders. It CHANGES THE REASONING behind the wet-lab DO-NOT-USE rule without changing the rule. The old wording was 'there is no wet lab here' — but a biotech founder plausibly DOES have FASTQs, instruments and single-cell data, so a session could wrongly conclude nextflow-development / instrument-data-to-allotrope / scvi-tools / single-cell-rna-qc now apply. THEY DO NOT. The boundary is not whether the CLIENT has a lab; it is what this business sells: desk research over public biomedical databases, not CRO or bioinformatics services. Running a founder's pipelines would carry no wet-lab QMS, no method validation, and would sit ENTIRELY OUTSIDE the citation-integrity guarantee the product rests on. WHAT DOES serve a founder are two of this plugin's unregistered servers: BioRender (figures for the SBIR/STTR application itself — a recurring founder need) and Wiley (paywalled full text for prior-work sections). That is the concrete bridge, and it reinforces the authorize order Wiley -> BioRender -> Synapse. Operating summary lives in the trinc-founder plugin (skill: founder-fit).
bio-research.LIVE_VERIFICATION_2026-07-29: Tools CALLED, not assumed. WORKING: pubmed (returned real PMIDs 42530074/42512343, 2870 hits); chembl (CHEMBL810 temozolomide, approved 1999, full molecular properties); c-trials (275 TERMINATED glioblastoma trials with real NCT ids); consensus (returned 3 papers but is CAPPED AT 3 RESULTS without a free Consensus account); biorxiv (tool schemas present). DEGRADED: ot / Open Targets returned 'Rate limit exceeded for client: global' — throttled at the shared-client level, so unreliable even as a chat-side duplicate. NOT WORKING — ZERO TOOLS EXPOSED: wiley, biorender, synapse, benchling. An unauthenticated server exposes no tools at all; a ToolSearch for them returns nothing. THEREFORE, THE HONEST STATE TODAY: the five servers that work (pubmed, chembl, c-trials, ot, owkin) all DUPLICATE existing subprocess-mcp engine adapters, so they add nothing the engine does not already have; and the three that justify keeping the plugin (wiley, biorender, synapse) currently contribute NOTHING because they are unauthenticated. The KEEP verdict therefore stands as a BET ON FUTURE OAUTH, not as current value. If the operator does not intend to authorize Wiley/BioRender/Synapse, the correct action is to drop the plugin — reinstalling later is trivial (it is a marketplace plugin). Do not describe this plugin as adding capability today.

oauth_posture.sanitize_dont_guard: THE ACTUAL RESOLUTION (2026-07-28). Rounds of work went into containing the engineering plugin's ungated github server — deny rules, an audit check, a rejected network block — when the right move was to remove the server instead of guarding it. No engineering skill references any MCP tool, and 8 of its 10 servers map to categories that resolve to NONE here, so the whole surface was liability with no upside. Fix: a sanitized local build at ~/.claude/local-plugins/engineering/ (marketplace `trinc-local`, v1.2.0-trinc.1) with .mcp.json deleted — skills byte-identical, `claude plugin details engineering` reports 'Skills (10) ... MCP servers (0)'. GENERALIZE THIS: when a plugin's value is its skills and its bundled MCP servers bind to tools this business does not have, sanitize the package rather than accumulate mitigations around it. The deny rules and gate-shadow audit stay regardless — they catch the NEXT plugin, one nobody has sanitized yet.
oauth_posture.why_no_redirect: The operator asked whether the engineering plugin could be pointed at the YubiKey-gated host GitHub MCP instead of the one it ships. It cannot, and the reason is structural: plugin MCP servers are namespaced `mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__*` while host servers are `mcp__<server>__*`, so a host server NEVER shadows a same-named plugin server — they coexist as separate surfaces. There is no alias, redirect, or override mechanism. Editing the plugin's .mcp.json is not an option either: the package is session-scoped and cloud-synced (see why_repo_owned). So the enforceable posture is: leave the plugin's github server unauthenticated, DENY its tools in ~/.claude/settings.json, and keep the host wrapper as the only GitHub path. No capability is lost — this monorepo is local-only with no git remote (~~source control), and the engineering plugin's value is its SKILLS, which need no MCP server at all.
